tracks.title: Your First Trip to China
tracks.ru: For those who haven't studied Chinese: phrases you can show on your screen and tried-and-true survival tips

topics.title: Before You Go: Visa, Money, Apps
topics.intro: This topic is your checklist before takeoff: which documents to bring, which apps to install and set up at home, how much cash to take, and how to stay connected. Plus six phrases that will help you from the very first minute, even if you don't know a single word of Chinese.

phrases.note: Works for everyone, anytime. It's more polite with older people: 您好 (nín hǎo).
They'll answer: 不客气 (bú kèqi), meaning “you're welcome.”
You can simply show this phrase on your screen. People will often reply 没关系 (méi guānxi), meaning “no problem.”
In short: 俄罗斯 (Éluósī) means “Russia.”
Show it on your screen and point right away at what you need help with: an address, a ticket, the cash desk.
Hold out your phone or a notebook: whatever is written down is easy to run through a translator.
The answer to the question about the purpose of your trip, at the border and at the hotel.
免签 (miǎnqiān) means “visa-free.” Handy at the hotel and with the police.
护照 (hùzhào) means passport. You'll be asked for it at the border, at hotels, and when buying a SIM card or tickets.
支付宝 (Zhīfùbǎo) — Alipay.
微信 (Wēixìn) is WeChat. In short: 微信 (Wēixìn).
现金 (xiànjīn) means cash. You can simply show a banknote.
In short: 换钱 (huàn qián) means “exchange money,” plus a questioning look.
电话卡 (diànhuàkǎ) means SIM card. They'll answer: 要护照 (yào hùzhào), meaning “passport needed.”
In China, people say Wi-Fi in English or 无线网 (wúxiànwǎng).

phrases.py: Wǒ de shǒujī méi diàn le.
phrases.note: In short: 没电了 (méi diàn le) means “it's out of power”; show your phone.

phrases.ru: Where can I get a power bank?
phrases.note: 充电宝 (chōngdiànbǎo) means power bank. They're often rented out via a QR code in cafés and shops.
You'll hear this from a driver or a passerby. Show the address on your screen.
You'll hear this at the border, at hotels, and at train stations. Just hand over your passport.
You'll hear this at the checkout: the seller will point to the QR code.
A common reply to “sorry” and to “I don't speak Chinese.”

dialogue.zh: 你好！你是第一次来中国吗？
dialogue.py: Nǐ hǎo! Nǐ shì dì-yī cì lái Zhōngguó ma?
dialogue.ru: Hi! Is this your first time going to China?

dialogue.zh: 是的。我不会说中文。
dialogue.py: Shì de. Wǒ bú huì shuō Zhōngwén.
dialogue.ru: Yes. I don't speak Chinese.

dialogue.zh: 没关系。你有支付宝吗？
dialogue.py: Méi guānxi. Nǐ yǒu Zhīfùbǎo ma?
dialogue.ru: No problem. Do you have Alipay?

dialogue.zh: 有，我绑了银行卡。
dialogue.py: Yǒu, wǒ bǎng le yínhángkǎ.
dialogue.ru: Yes, I linked a bank card.

dialogue.zh: 很好。现金也带一点儿吧。
dialogue.py: Hěn hǎo. Xiànjīn yě dài yìdiǎnr ba.
dialogue.ru: Great. Take a little cash too.

dialogue.zh: 好的。哪里可以买电话卡？
dialogue.py: Hǎo de. Nǎli kěyǐ mǎi diànhuàkǎ?
dialogue.ru: Okay. Where can I buy a SIM card?

dialogue.zh: 机场就有，要带护照。
dialogue.py: Jīchǎng jiù yǒu, yào dài hùzhào.
dialogue.ru: Right at the airport; you need to bring your passport.

dialogue.zh: 谢谢！
dialogue.py: Xièxie!
dialogue.ru: Thank you!

dialogue.zh: 不客气，一路顺风！
dialogue.py: Bú kèqi, yílù shùnfēng!
dialogue.ru: You're welcome, have a good trip!

topics.culture: In China almost everything is paid for with your phone via QR code: Alipay and WeChat Pay work in the metro and at street stalls alike, so it's worth installing and setting them up at home, while you still have your usual internet and the SMS messages from your bank. At the same time, businesses are legally required to accept cash, and a small stash of yuan is the best insurance against a dead phone or a connection failure. Many familiar services (Google, WhatsApp, Instagram) don't open through the local internet, and WeChat will be the main messenger for everyone. Chinese people gladly help tourists: a phrase on your screen, a smile, and a translator in your phone solve most problems.

tips.t: Russian citizens with a regular international passport can enter without a visa for tourism, business, visiting relatives and friends, exchanges, and transit, and stay in China for up to 30 days in a row (counting from the day after entry). The rule is in effect until December 31, 2027.

tips.h: When you still need a visa
tips.t: The visa-free option doesn't cover work, study, or journalism. The 30 visa-free days can't be extended: if you need to stay longer, you apply to the immigration service for permission. You can enter visa-free multiple times.

Your passport must be valid for the whole length of your trip. Keep your return ticket and your hotel booking or invitation on your phone: a border officer may ask about the purpose of your trip. Insurance isn't required for visa-free entry, but medical care in China is paid, so it's better to buy it.
Before you fly, install and set up Alipay and WeChat (payments, taxi and delivery mini-programs), Amap (高德) or Baidu Maps, and Trip.com for hotels and tickets. Alipay has a built-in translator.
Alipay and WeChat Pay accept foreign Visa and Mastercard cards; WeChat Pay also accepts Diners Club and JCB, and Alipay accepts Diners Club and Discover. Mir cards are not on these lists.

Visa and Mastercard cards issued by Russian banks don't work abroad. UnionPay cards from some Russian banks can sometimes be linked, but there are no official guarantees: check with your bank and don't rely on them alone.
Bring a supply of yuan: they'll save you if your phone or connection fails. Without a declaration you can bring in up to 20,000 yuan and foreign currency up to the equivalent of 5,000 US dollars.

SIM cards are sold with a passport at major airports and at China Mobile, China Unicom, and China Telecom stores. If you want to keep your Russian number, check the roaming terms and prices in China with your carrier before you fly.

tips.h: No 3C, no power bank on board
tips.t: Since June 28, 2025, power banks without a 3C mark, with an unreadable mark, or from recalled batches are not allowed on domestic flights in China. A power bank bought in Russia usually doesn't have this mark.

Spring Festival (Chinese New Year) in 2027 falls on February 6; during those weeks tickets and hotels get more expensive and sell out quickly. The exact days off for 2027 are announced separately by China's State Council: check on gov.cn.

quiz.q: How many days in a row can a Russian citizen stay in China without a visa?
quiz.explain: Up to 30 days in a row, counting from the day after entry; the rule is in effect until 12/31/2027.

quiz.q: For what purpose is visa-free entry NOT suitable?
quiz.explain: Work, study, and journalism require a visa.

quiz.q: How do you say “I don't speak Chinese”?
quiz.explain: 不会说 means “can't speak,” 中文 means the Chinese language.

quiz.q: Which card are you most likely to be able to link to Alipay?
options: A Visa from a Russian bank
A Visa or Mastercard from a foreign bank
quiz.explain: Alipay and WeChat Pay accept Visa and Mastercard from foreign banks; Mir is not supported, and Visa/Mastercard from Russian banks don't work abroad.

Say that you don't speak Chinese
Say that you're coming as a tourist
Ask about payment: Alipay, WeChat Pay, or cash
Ask where to buy a SIM card

topics.title: Arrival: Border, Airport, and Your First Day
topics.intro: After this topic you'll calmly get through passport control and customs, understand the border officer's short questions, and get from the airport to your hotel. The main secret is to fill out the arrival card in advance and save your hotel's address in Chinese.

phrases.note: The answer to the border officer's question about the purpose of your trip.
Show your booking with the hotel's address in Chinese.
Put in your own number of days; you can show it on your fingers.

phrases.ru: Please take me to this address.
phrases.note: For the taxi driver: show the address on your screen.
In short: 出租车？(chūzūchē?) Look for the “Taxi” sign.
In short: 地铁？(dìtiě?) The sign says “Metro.”

phrases.py: Wǒ méiyǒu yào shēnbào de dōngxi.
phrases.note: Then take the green channel 无申报通道 (wú shēnbào tōngdào).

phrases.ru: Where do I pick up my luggage?
phrases.note: The sign says 行李提取 (xíngli tíqǔ), “Baggage Claim.”
Show your baggage tag at the lost-luggage desk in the baggage claim hall.

phrases.ru: Where can I buy a SIM card?
phrases.note: They'll most likely answer with a gesture; look for the China Mobile, China Unicom, and China Telecom counters.
流量 (liúliàng) means mobile internet data.
The sign says 外币兑换 (wàibì duìhuàn), “Currency Exchange.”

phrases.ru: I need to get back to my hotel.
phrases.note: Keep the hotel's business card with the address in Chinese.
You'll hear this from the border officer. Hold out your passport.

phrases.ru: Why have you come to China?
phrases.note: You'll hear this. The answer: 我来旅游 (Wǒ lái lǚyóu).
You'll hear this. Show your hotel booking.

phrases.ru: How many days will you stay?
phrases.note: You'll hear this. Say the number or show your return ticket.
You'll hear this: look into the camera for your photo.

phrases.ru: Place your fingers on the scanner.
phrases.note: You'll hear this at the fingerprint scanner.

phrases.ru: Do you have anything to declare?
phrases.note: You'll hear this at customs. The answer: 没有 (méiyǒu), meaning “no.”
You'll hear this. The answer: 谢谢！(Xièxie!)

dialogue.zh: 你好，请出示护照和入境卡。
dialogue.py: Nǐ hǎo, qǐng chūshì hùzhào hé rùjìngkǎ.
dialogue.ru: Hello, please show your passport and arrival card.

dialogue.zh: 你好。这是我的护照，入境卡我在网上填了。
dialogue.py: Nǐ hǎo. Zhè shì wǒ de hùzhào, rùjìngkǎ wǒ zài wǎngshàng tián le.
dialogue.ru: Hello. Here is my passport; I filled out the arrival card online.

dialogue.zh: 来中国做什么？
dialogue.py: Lái Zhōngguó zuò shénme?
dialogue.ru: Why have you come to China?

dialogue.zh: 我来旅游。
dialogue.py: Wǒ lái lǚyóu.
dialogue.ru: I'm a tourist.

dialogue.zh: 待几天？住在哪里？
dialogue.py: Dāi jǐ tiān? Zhù zài nǎli?
dialogue.ru: How many days will you stay? Where will you be staying?

dialogue.zh: 七天。我住这个酒店。
dialogue.py: Qī tiān. Wǒ zhù zhège jiǔdiàn.
dialogue.ru: Seven days. I'm staying at this hotel.

dialogue.zh: 好。看这里，按一下指纹。
dialogue.py: Hǎo. Kàn zhèli, àn yíxià zhǐwén.
dialogue.ru: Okay. Look here and place your fingers on the scanner.

dialogue.zh: 好的。
dialogue.py: Hǎo de.
dialogue.ru: Okay.

dialogue.zh: 可以了。欢迎来中国！
dialogue.py: Kěyǐ le. Huānyíng lái Zhōngguó!
dialogue.ru: Done. Welcome to China!

topics.culture: Border and customs control in China is quick and businesslike: the questions are short, and the signs in major airports are also in English. Don't worry if the border officer speaks only Chinese: they usually ask the purpose of your trip, how many days you'll stay, and where you'll be staying, and you can show the answer on your phone screen. After customs, don't accept offers of a “ride” in the arrivals hall: follow the signs to the official taxi queue, the metro, or the buses. The first thing to do in the city is to save your hotel's address in Chinese and pick up its business card; it's your “ticket home” for any taxi driver.

tips.t: Since November 20, 2025, a foreigner's arrival card can be filled out before the trip: on the website s.nia.gov.cn/ArrivalCardFillingPC, in the NIA 12367 app, or in the mini-program in WeChat and Alipay. If you didn't get to it, fill it out at the border via QR code, at a terminal, or on paper.

The border officer may ask about the purpose of your trip, the length of your stay, and where you'll be staying; keep your hotel booking and return ticket on your phone. Foreigners are fingerprinted on entry.
If you have nothing to declare, you don't need to fill out a form: take the green channel “无申报通道.” If you have something to declare, fill out the declaration and go to the red channel “申报通道.”
Without a declaration you can bring in up to 20,000 yuan and foreign currency up to the equivalent of 5,000 US dollars per person. Anything more must be declared in writing.
Animals and plants and products made from them are items that must be declared at customs. It's easier not to bring meat, dairy products, fresh fruit, or seeds.
Beijing airports have free Wi-Fi; without a Chinese phone number, a machine prints the login and password if you scan your passport. At other airports the procedure may differ.

tips.h: A SIM card right on arrival
tips.t: Major airports (Beijing, Shanghai Pudong, Guangzhou Baiyun) have carrier counters: SIM cards are issued with your passport. A Chinese number is needed for SMS codes, including for public Wi-Fi.

tips.h: How to get to your hotel
tips.t: The most reliable options are the metro, a shuttle bus, or a taxi from the official queue, following the “Taxi” signs. Drivers hardly speak English, so show your hotel's address in Chinese.
In the arrivals halls of Beijing airports there are information desks and payment service centers: they'll help with Wi-Fi and with setting up Alipay and WeChat.
The hotline of the National Immigration Administration, 12367, also answers in Russian: choose your language in the voice menu, and an interpreter will be connected to your call.

quiz.q: The border officer asks: “来中国做什么？” What should you answer?
quiz.explain: 来中国做什么 means “why have you come to China.” 我来旅游 means “I'm a tourist.”

quiz.q: You have nothing to declare. Where do you go at customs?
options: To the red channel “申报通道”
To the green channel “无申报通道”
quiz.explain: If you have nothing to declare, you don't need a form; just walk through the green channel.

quiz.q: Above what amount of cash yuan must they be declared on entry?
quiz.explain: Without a declaration you can bring in up to 20,000 yuan; foreign currency, up to the equivalent of 5,000 US dollars.

quiz.q: When can you fill out the arrival card?
options: In advance online or at the border
quiz.explain: Since 11/20/2025 the card can be filled out in advance online (website, NIA 12367 app, mini-programs), and at the border via QR code or on paper.

Say that you're a tourist

topics.title: First Words: Hello, Thank You, I Don't Understand
topics.intro: A dozen words that will keep you from getting lost: greet someone, thank them, apologize, and honestly say “I don't understand.” Most phrases can simply be shown on your phone screen; Chinese people are used to this and gladly help.

phrases.note: Works for everyone, anytime. To an older person you can say it more politely: 您好 (Nín hǎo).
In reply you'll hear 不客气 (bú kèqi) or 不用谢 (bú yòng xiè), meaning “you're welcome.”

phrases.ru: Excuse me (pardon me, may I ask…).
phrases.note: A soft “excuse me” for getting a person's attention, squeezing past, or apologizing lightly.
Literally “I hear, but I don't understand.” You can also say it while pointing to your ear and shaking your head.
It instantly takes away the awkwardness: the other person will start gesturing or take out their phone.
Show this phrase and hold out your own phone with the translator open.

phrases.ru: Yes, that's right. / No, that's wrong.
phrases.note: This is how you answer the question “did I understand correctly?” A nod is understood too.

phrases.ru: I need it (yes, I'll take it). / I don't need it.
phrases.note: The most useful “no”: for pushy sellers, a bag at the checkout, an extra service.
A universal “yes.”
For when you're really at fault: you bumped into someone or were late. The reply: 没关系 (méi guānxi), meaning “no problem.”
The answers: 会一点 (huì yìdiǎn), meaning “a little,” 不会 (bú huì), meaning “no.” Young people are more likely to help.

phrases.ru: Excuse me, could you tell me…
phrases.note: The start of any question to a stranger; after it you can show a picture or an address.
Say it and point with your finger; in a shop or café that's often enough.
Kazakhstan is 哈萨克斯坦 (Hāsàkèsītǎn), Belarus is 白俄罗斯 (Bái'éluósī).
Put in your own name. Ivan is 伊万 (Yīwàn).
Young people often say 拜拜 (báibái), meaning “bye.”
You'll hear this often. The answer: 我是俄罗斯人。
You'll hear this if you weren't understood. Show the phrase on your screen or in the translator.

phrases.py: Nǐ Zhōngwén shuō de hěn hǎo!
phrases.note: People will say this even for a single “nǐhǎo.” A modest reply: 哪里哪里 (nǎli nǎli), or you can simply say 谢谢。

dialogue.zh: 不好意思，请问，你会说英语吗？
dialogue.py: Bù hǎoyìsi, qǐngwèn, nǐ huì shuō Yīngyǔ ma?
dialogue.ru: Excuse me, do you speak English?

dialogue.zh: 不会。你是哪国人？
dialogue.py: Bú huì. Nǐ shì nǎ guó rén?
dialogue.ru: No. Which country are you from?

dialogue.zh: 我是俄罗斯人。我不会说中文。
dialogue.py: Wǒ shì Éluósīrén. Wǒ bú huì shuō Zhōngwén.
dialogue.ru: I'm from Russia. I don't speak Chinese.

dialogue.zh: 没关系！你要去哪儿？
dialogue.py: Méi guānxi! Nǐ yào qù nǎr?
dialogue.ru: No problem! Where do you need to go?

dialogue.zh: 对不起，我听不懂。请用手机翻译。
dialogue.py: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ tīng bu dǒng. Qǐng yòng shǒujī fānyì.
dialogue.ru: Sorry, I don't understand. Please translate on your phone.

dialogue.zh: 好的。你要去地铁站吗？
dialogue.py: Hǎo de. Nǐ yào qù dìtiězhàn ma?
dialogue.ru: Okay. Do you need to get to the metro?

dialogue.zh: 对！谢谢！
dialogue.py: Duì! Xièxie!
dialogue.ru: Yes! Thank you!

dialogue.zh: 不客气。那边，一直走。
dialogue.py: Bú kèqi. Nàbiān, yìzhí zǒu.
dialogue.ru: You're welcome. That way, straight ahead all the time.

dialogue.zh: 谢谢，再见！
dialogue.py: Xièxie, zàijiàn!
dialogue.ru: Thank you, goodbye!

topics.culture: People in China gladly help a foreigner who doesn't know Chinese: a passerby will sooner take out a phone with a translator than brush you off. Speak briefly, smile, show your screen; this is normal and isn't considered rude. 不好意思 opens almost any conversation, and 谢谢 is worth saying more often than seems necessary. Don't be surprised by direct questions: where you're from, how old you are, whether you're married; it's ordinary curiosity, and you can answer with a smile. Loud speech on the street and in cafés isn't aggression, just the usual manner.

tips.t: Take screenshots of the main phrases and your hotel's address in characters. Showing your screen is the fastest way to get your point across.
Install a translator that works in China in advance: the official guide for foreigners names Youdao (有道) and Baidu Translate (百度翻译). Test it before your trip.
In airports and large hotels English is understood more often; on the street, in cafés, and in taxis, rarely. Count on your phone and gestures.

In Beijing the city line 12345 connects you to an operator in a foreign language; among its 8 languages is Russian. Other cities have their own sets of languages: for example, in Zhejiang, 12345 offers English on weekdays from 8:30 to 17:30.
Police: 110, fire: 119, ambulance: 120, traffic accidents: 122. Calls are free throughout the country.
Save your hotel's name and address in Chinese (a business card from the front desk or a screenshot). Taxi drivers and passersby often can't read Latin letters.
Say 不好意思 or 你好; that's enough. Don't wave your hand or touch the person's shoulder.
To personal questions (age, salary, family) you can answer with a smile: 还可以 (hái kěyǐ), meaning “so-so.” There's no need to take offense.

quiz.q: Someone is speaking to you quickly and you understand nothing. What do you say?
quiz.explain: 我听不懂 means “I don't understand (by ear).” Then you can ask: 请用手机翻译。

quiz.q: Someone said “谢谢” to you. How do you reply?
quiz.explain: 不客气 means “you're welcome.” 不用谢 works too.

quiz.q: How do you politely ask a passerby a question?
quiz.explain: 不好意思，请问…… means “excuse me, could you tell me…”

quiz.q: What number do you call for the police in China?
quiz.explain: 110 is the police, 120 is an ambulance, 119 is the fire department, 122 is traffic accidents.

role.ai_role: a passerby on a street in Beijing, friendly; speaks very slowly and in short HSK 1 level phrases, gladly repeats and offers to translate on the phone
role.user_goal: greet someone, say that you're from Russia and don't speak Chinese, ask them to speak more slowly, say thank you and goodbye
role.opening: 你好！你是哪国人？
checklist: Say hello (你好)
Say where you're from (我是俄罗斯人)
Say that you don't speak or don't understand Chinese
Ask them to speak more slowly or repeat
Say thank you and goodbye

topics.title: Numbers, Prices, and Gestures
topics.intro: The numbers from 1 to 10, hundreds, and thousands are enough to understand a price at the market, the total at the checkout, and a bus number. You'll learn how to show a number on your fingers the Chinese way and how not to mix up 150 and 105.

phrases.note: Point at the item and the question is clear.
When counting, 一 is read yī; in combinations the tone changes (yì bǎi, yí wàn).
11 = 十一 (shíyī), 20 = 二十 (èrshí), 35 = 三十五 (sānshíwǔ).
The most reliable way to find out a price: the seller writes it down or types it on a calculator.

phrases.ru: How much is it in total?

phrases.note: When counting objects, “two” is 两 (liǎng), not 二: 两个、两位、两斤.
块 (kuài) is the colloquial word for “yuan.” Price tags use 元 or ¥.
毛 (máo) is 0.1 yuan: 五毛 = 0.5 yuan.
Not 105! “One hundred five” is 一百零五 (yìbǎi líng wǔ). 零 (líng) is zero.
People also say 二百 (èrbǎi); both versions are correct.
Chinese counts in tens of thousands: 两万 = 20,000, 十万 = 100,000.
斤 (jīn) is 500 g. At the market the price is almost always quoted per jin.
折 is the share of the price: 八折 = you pay 80%, 五折 = half price.
八点 (bā diǎn) — 8:00, 八点半 (bā diǎn bàn) — 8:30.
In phone numbers and room numbers, one is read yāo: 138 = yāo sān bā.
3号线 (sān hào xiàn) is metro line No. 3.
You'll hear this at the checkout. If you didn't understand, ask: 请写一下。
You'll hear this from the seller. You can answer with your fingers.
You'll hear this if you pay with a large banknote.
You'll hear this when paying: the seller points at the QR code.

dialogue.zh: 你好，这个多少钱？
dialogue.py: Nǐ hǎo, zhège duōshao qián?
dialogue.ru: Hello, how much is this?

dialogue.zh: 十二块一斤。
dialogue.py: Shí'èr kuài yì jīn.
dialogue.ru: Twelve yuan per jin.

dialogue.zh: 一斤？请写一下。
dialogue.py: Yì jīn? Qǐng xiě yíxià.
dialogue.ru: Per jin? Please write it down.

dialogue.zh: 好，你看。你要几斤？
dialogue.py: Hǎo, nǐ kàn. Nǐ yào jǐ jīn?
dialogue.ru: Okay, look. How many jin will you take?

dialogue.zh: 两斤。
dialogue.py: Liǎng jīn.
dialogue.ru: Two jin.

dialogue.zh: 两斤，一共二十四块。
dialogue.py: Liǎng jīn, yígòng èrshísì kuài.
dialogue.ru: Two jin, twenty-four yuan in total.

dialogue.zh: 二十四？好的。可以扫码吗？
dialogue.py: Èrshísì? Hǎo de. Kěyǐ sǎomǎ ma?
dialogue.ru: Twenty-four? Okay. Can I pay with a QR code?

topics.culture: In China, numbers are more than counting. 8 (bā) sounds like “to get rich” and is considered lucky, so people love it in prices, phone numbers, and license plates. 4 (sì) sounds like “death” (sǐ): some buildings and hotels have no 4th or 14th floor. At the market the price is quoted per 斤 (half a kilo), not per kilogram, and the amount is often said without the word “yuan”: “三十五” means 35 yuan. For the numbers 6 to 10 there are their own one-handed gestures, and they're easy to mix up with the ones you're used to.

tips.t: 6 is the thumb and little finger; 7 is a pinch of fingertips; 8 is the thumb and index finger in an L shape; 9 is the index finger bent like a hook; 10 is a fist or two crossed index fingers. The gestures are described from reference sources; there are local variations, especially for 7–10.
For 7–10 different regions have their own variants, and the two-finger “L” may be understood by a visitor as 2. If the amount matters, ask the person to write it down or show it on a calculator.
斤 (jīn) is a traditional unit of weight, 500 g. A price of “10 yuan per jin” means 20 yuan per kilogram (公斤).
The price tag says 元 or ¥, and out loud people more often say 块 (kuài). One tenth of a yuan is 角 on the price tag and 毛 (máo) out loud.
Large sums are counted in 万 (10,000): 3万 is 30,000, not 3,000. Check the zeros, especially with rent and big purchases.
A price tag of 7折 means “you pay 70%,” that is, a 30% discount. The smaller the number before 折, the bigger the discount.
In phone, room, or bus numbers, 1 is often read yāo so it isn't confused with 7 (qī). If you hear “yāo,” it means one.
Since February 1, 2026, a People's Bank of China rule is in effect: sellers may not refuse cash yuan, except where the law requires cashless payment. Keep small bills on you.

quiz.explain: 折 is the share of the full price: 八折 = 80% of the price.

quiz.explain: 一百五 is short for 一百五十 (150). 105 is 一百零五.

quiz.q: How do you say “two pieces”?
quiz.explain: Before a measure word, “two” is 两: 两个.

topics.culture: In China people pay by phone almost everywhere: in shops, taxis, the metro, and at street stalls. There are two ways: the seller scans your payment code (付款码) or you scan their QR code and enter the amount yourself, which is why at the checkout you're often asked “你扫我还是我扫你？”. The money arrives instantly, and the seller expects you to show the confirmation screen. Businesses are legally required to accept cash, but there can be trouble with change, so small bills come in handy. The traveler's main rule is to always carry two ways to pay: an app with a linked card and a little yuan.

tips.t: Foreign Visa and Mastercard cards can be linked to Alipay and WeChat Pay; WeChat Pay also accepts Diners Club and JCB, and Alipay accepts Diners Club and Discover. Mir cards are not on the lists.

Visa and Mastercard cards issued by Russian banks don't work abroad. UnionPay cards from some Russian banks can sometimes be linked, but there is no official confirmation, so check with your bank in advance and bring a backup option.
Since 2024, foreigners have had a mobile payment limit of up to 5,000 US dollars per transaction and up to 50,000 dollars per year. Check the current limits for your own account in the app.
WeChat Pay doesn't charge the 3% fee on a foreign card for a payment under 200 yuan. Alipay has its own terms, so check the amount on the screen before confirming.
“你扫我” means you scan the seller's QR and enter the amount; “我扫你” means the seller scans your 付款码. If one doesn't work, try the other.
According to an announcement by the People's Bank of China, refusing to accept cash yuan is illegal. But there may be no change, so keep small bills.
Currency is exchanged at banks and exchange offices with the appropriate sign. You can withdraw yuan from an ATM that shows the logo of your card's payment system, if it's a card from a foreign bank.
In the “Transport” section of Alipay you can turn on a QR code for riding the metro: the fare is charged to your linked card. This works, for example, in Beijing.

If in one day, in one store marked “退税” (Tax Free), you buy goods worth 200 yuan or more, you can get the VAT refunded when you leave; in some stores the money is returned right at the time of purchase. Bring your passport.
Keep two ways to pay on your phone and a little cash in your wallet: the connection, the battery, or the bank can let you down at the most inconvenient moment.

topics.culture: The Chinese internet lives in its own apps: WeChat replaces messengers and social networks, Alipay is your wallet and your way into taxis, delivery, and tickets, and Amap (高德) and Baidu Maps replace the maps you're used to. Many foreign services, including Google, YouTube, Instagram, and WhatsApp, don't open through the local internet, so agree in advance with your loved ones on how you'll stay in touch. Public Wi-Fi often asks for an SMS code sent to a Chinese number, and a local SIM card makes life much easier. Chinese people are happy to communicate through a translator on your phone: just hold up your phone and smile.

tips.h: A SIM card with your passport
tips.t: SIM cards are sold at China Mobile, China Unicom, and China Telecom stores and at counters in major airports; they're issued with your passport. Plans include calls and limited data.

A local eSIM in mainland China can't be activated on all phones (for example, on the iPhone Air it can). If your phone supports eSIM, you can buy a regional eSIM from an international provider in advance; check compatibility before your trip.
A Russian SIM card in roaming works through your carrier's network. Check availability, prices, and plans for China with your carrier before you fly.
Free Wi-Fi in China often sends a code by SMS to a Chinese number, and the code may not arrive on a foreign one. That's why a local SIM card makes life much easier.

Google, YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp are not directly accessible through the local internet; Telegram generally doesn't work either. Agree with your loved ones on staying in touch via WeChat.
Chinese maps are Amap (高德) and Baidu Maps; the interface is mostly in Chinese, but in Amap you can search by an address in English. Save your hotel's address in Chinese to show it to the driver.
Alipay has a built-in translator for 15 languages. Check in advance whether the language pair you need is among them, and keep a backup translator with an offline mode.
Alipay has mini-programs for DiDi (taxis), Trip.com, and delivery services, so you don't have to install separate apps.
Power banks without a 3C mark or with an unreadable mark are not allowed on domestic flights in China (a rule since June 28, 2025). In the city you can rent a power bank via a QR code.
You can ask questions about visas and registration at 12367 (the National Immigration Administration): the voice menu includes Russian.

quiz.q: Which app should you use in China to stay in touch with Chinese people?
quiz.explain: WeChat is China's main messenger; WhatsApp, Instagram, and Google services are not available through the local internet.

topics.culture: In Chinese cities you almost always call a car through an app: DiDi or the taxi section in Alipay and WeChat. The driver often calls before pickup to find out where you're standing; if you don't understand, write to them in the app's chat. Before getting in, check the license plate against the app, and the driver will check the last digits of your phone number (尾号). You usually sit in the back, and tipping isn't customary. At airports and train stations, app-booked cars pick up in a separate zone: follow the 网约车 (wǎngyuēchē) signs and don't accept offers from people in the arrivals hall.

tips.t: The DiDi app has an English interface: you can register with a foreign phone number, link an international bank card, and chat with the driver using built-in translation.

tips.h: Taxis straight from Alipay and WeChat
tips.t: A separate app isn't necessary: in Alipay open Transport → Taxi, in WeChat open Services → Mobility (Ride Hailing).

tips.h: Set everything up before your trip
tips.t: Register and link your payment method in advance, while still at home: doing it on the street with no internet and a suitcase is inconvenient. Check whether your card works with a test payment.
Before getting in, check the license plate and the driver's details in the app. Use only official and well-known platforms.
Save your hotel's address in characters (from the booking or the hotel's business card) and enter the destination through the app's search. The driver may not understand an address in English.

You flag down a free taxi with a wave of your hand, but not every one will stop: some cars are already heading to a customer from the app. So when you're short on time, it's more reliable to call a car through an app.
Don't panic: say 我不会说中文 and write in the app's chat. There you can send a message with translation or your own location.
Open the completed trip in the app's history and contact the driver or support. In a taxi from the street, take a receipt (发票, fāpiào) or photograph the license plate.
Look for your app-booked car in the pickup zone shown by the app and the 网约车 signs. It's better to politely decline “taxi” offers from people in the arrivals hall.

dialogue.ru: This one (shows the order on the phone).

dialogue.zh: A12检票口，在二楼。
dialogue.py: A shí'èr jiǎnpiàokǒu, zài èr lóu.
dialogue.ru: Gate A12, on the second floor.

dialogue.zh: 我用护照，走哪个通道？
dialogue.py: Wǒ yòng hùzhào, zǒu nǎge tōngdào?
dialogue.ru: I have a passport; which lane should I go through?

dialogue.zh: 走人工通道，就在旁边。
dialogue.py: Zǒu réngōng tōngdào, jiù zài pángbiān.
dialogue.ru: Through the lane with a staff member; it's right nearby.

dialogue.zh: 好的，谢谢！
dialogue.py: Hǎo de, xièxie!
dialogue.ru: Okay, thank you!

dialogue.zh: 不客气。快检票了，别晚了。
dialogue.py: Bú kèqi. Kuài jiǎnpiào le, bié wǎn le.
dialogue.ru: You're welcome. Boarding will start soon, don't be late.

topics.culture: Trains in China are a fast and convenient way to travel between cities, but your ticket is tied to your passport, so everything at the station revolves around it: a document check at the entrance, a baggage check, then the waiting hall and the boarding gate (检票口). Boarding closes a few minutes before departure, so arrive early. Big cities have several stations (北站, 南站, 东站, 西站: North, South, East, West), and they're easy to mix up: check the station name in your order. The metro entrance may also have a bag check, and it's best to find out the right station exit (A口, B口) in advance in your navigation app. On major holidays tickets sell out fast, so buy as early as possible.

tips.t: Train tickets are sold on the official website and in the 12306 app (there's an English version), as well as at station ticket offices. A foreigner first needs to pass an identity check with a passport: without it you can't buy a ticket.
If the automatic passport check didn't go through, you can upload a photo of your passport page for a manual check, which usually takes 3–5 working days. So register on 12306 before your trip.

tips.h: Name exactly as in the passport
tips.t: Most often the check fails because of mistakes in the name and passport details. Enter everything letter for letter, as on the photo page.

You don't need a paper ticket: you enter the station with the same document that the ticket was bought with. With a passport, go to the lane with a manual check (人工通道), where a staff member will check your passport and ticket.

China's official tourism portal advises arriving at the station at least 30 minutes before departure: boarding closes shortly before the train leaves. Allowing for the queue at the check and the baggage screening, it's better to plan for more.
You can change or return a ticket in the 12306 app or at the station ticket office. The fee depends on how much time is left before departure; the app will show the exact amount before you confirm.

There is a metro in 55 cities in China. A single-ride ticket is sold at machines and ticket offices; you can pay with cash yuan, bank cards, or mobile apps. In Alipay the QR code for the metro is in the Transport section, after an identity check.

tips.h: Beijing: card right at the turnstile
tips.t: In Beijing you can go through the metro turnstile by tapping a foreign-issued Visa or Mastercard on it. Check in advance that your card works abroad.
For questions about tickets and rules, call the China Railway hotline 12306 or use the 12306 app.

quiz.q: You bought a ticket on 12306 with your passport. What do you show at the station entrance?
quiz.explain: You go in with the same document that the ticket was bought with. A paper ticket isn't needed.

quiz.q: The automatic turnstile doesn't accept your passport. Where do you go?
options: To the ticket office to buy a new ticket
To 人工通道, the lane with a staff member
quiz.explain: 人工通道 is a lane where a staff member checks documents.

quiz.q: How many minutes before the train departs is it best to arrive at the station?
options: You can be late: the train will wait
quiz.explain: Boarding closes a few minutes before departure, and the entrance still has a check and baggage screening.

quiz.q: How do you ask in the metro where the transfer is?
quiz.explain: 换乘 means transfer. 检票口 is the boarding gate for the train, 车厢 is a train car, 退票 means to return a ticket.

role.ai_role: Chína is a staff member at Beijing South Railway Station. She speaks very simply and slowly, in HSK 1–2 level phrases, points with her hand, and repeats if the passenger didn't understand.

topics.title: Food: Ordering, Allergies, Spicy
topics.intro: In a café you'll be able to say how many of you there are, order a dish by pointing at the menu or using a QR code, ask for it not spicy, and warn about allergies. You'll also learn which water to drink and whether you need to leave a tip.

phrases.note: Point at a picture in the menu: even Chinese people order that way.
The main phrase in Sichuan and Hunan. Say it when ordering each dish.
Instead of 花生 put in: 海鲜 (hǎixiān) for seafood, 鸡蛋 (jīdàn) for eggs, 牛奶 (niúnǎi) for milk, 坚果 (jiānguǒ) for nuts.
In many cafés you pay at the register or by QR code on the table.
A menu with pictures: 有图片的吗？(Yǒu túpiàn de ma?).
Point at the next table.
Even 微辣 in Sichuan can turn out to be very spicy.
Cilantro is put in almost everything.
牛肉 (niúròu) means beef. 我吃素 (Wǒ chī sù) means “I'm vegetarian,” but the broth or fat may be meat-based, so double-check.

phrases.ru: A bottle of drinking water, please.

phrases.note: Without this, drinks are often served at room temperature.

phrases.ru: Can I order by QR code?

phrases.note: 打包 also means “pack up the leftovers”: taking home what you haven't finished is normal.
You'll hear this at the entrance. You can simply show it with your fingers.
You'll hear and see this on the table: scan the code and the menu opens.
You'll hear this when ordering. The answer: 不要辣 or 微辣.
You'll hear this at fast-food places and cafés.

phrases.ru: What would you like to drink?
phrases.note: You'll hear this after ordering food.
You'll hear this from a waiter or cashier.

dialogue.zh: 欢迎光临！几位？
dialogue.py: Huānyíng guānglín! Jǐ wèi?
dialogue.ru: Welcome! How many of you?

dialogue.zh: 两位。有菜单吗？
dialogue.py: Liǎng wèi. Yǒu càidān ma?
dialogue.ru: Two. Do you have a menu?

dialogue.zh: 扫码点餐，桌上有二维码。
dialogue.py: Sǎomǎ diǎncān, zhuō shang yǒu èrwéimǎ.
dialogue.ru: Order by QR code; the code is on the table.

dialogue.zh: 我不会。我要这个和这个。
dialogue.py: Wǒ bú huì. Wǒ yào zhège hé zhège.
dialogue.ru: I can't. I'd like this and this.

dialogue.zh: 好的。要辣吗？
dialogue.py: Hǎo de. Yào là ma?
dialogue.ru: Okay. Spicy or not?

dialogue.zh: 不要辣。我对花生过敏。
dialogue.py: Bú yào là. Wǒ duì huāshēng guòmǐn.
dialogue.ru: Not spicy. I'm allergic to peanuts.

dialogue.zh: 好，不放花生。喝什么？
dialogue.py: Hǎo, bú fàng huāshēng. Hē shénme?
dialogue.ru: Okay, no peanuts. What would you like to drink?

dialogue.zh: 一瓶矿泉水，谢谢。
dialogue.py: Yì píng kuàngquánshuǐ, xièxie.
dialogue.ru: A bottle of water, thanks.

dialogue.zh: 好的，稍等。
dialogue.py: Hǎo de, shāo děng.
dialogue.ru: Okay, one moment.

topics.culture: In China, dishes are ordered for everyone and eaten from shared plates, and rice is often brought at the end; ask for it right away if you want it. Taking leftovers home (打包) is normal. You call the waiter out loud: 你好 or 服务员 (fúwùyuán); it isn't rude. At the start of a meal, hot water or tea is often poured for free. Don't stick chopsticks upright in rice: it resembles a funeral rite.

tips.t: In China tap water is drunk only boiled; you can brush your teeth with it at the hotel. Restaurants usually pour boiled water or tea, and a bottle of water in a shop costs about 2 yuan.
Make a card: “我对___过敏，请不要放” (I'm allergic to ___, please don't put it in) and show it with every order. A waiter may not take a spoken phrase seriously.

Mandatory labeling of eight allergen groups (gluten, crustaceans, fish, eggs, peanuts, soy, milk, nuts) is being introduced by a new label standard with a 2-year transition period, that is, from about 2027. Until then, packaging may not highlight them, so read the ingredients or ask.
微辣 in Sichuan, Hunan, or Chongqing may be spicier than you expect. If you can't have anything spicy at all, say 不要辣 and add 一点都不要 (yìdiǎn dōu bú yào), meaning “not at all.”
A menu by QR code opens in WeChat or Alipay. If it doesn't work, ask for a paper menu (有菜单吗) or point at a picture and say 这个.
In most restaurants and hotels tips are not expected. In bars and hotel cafés a 10–15% service charge may be added; it's already on the bill.
Under People's Bank of China rules in effect since February 1, 2026, cafés may not refuse cash yuan. A small amount in small bills will save you if phone payment doesn't go through.

For delivery, the official guide for foreigners names Meituan (美团), Taobao Instant Commerce (淘宝闪购), and JD (京东). The interface is mostly in Chinese, and the courier almost always calls, so ask a hotel employee to help with your first order.

quiz.q: Can you drink water straight from the tap?
quiz.explain: According to Beijing's tourism portal, tap water in China is drunk only after boiling.

quiz.q: The waiter asks “几位？”. What is he asking about?
options: What would you like to drink?
quiz.explain: 几位 means how many people. The answer: 两位 (two people) or show it with your fingers.

quiz.q: How do you ask for a dish to be not spicy?
quiz.explain: 不要辣 means “no spicy food.”

quiz.q: Do you need to leave a tip in an ordinary restaurant?
quiz.explain: Shanghai's official portal: in most restaurants and hotels, tips are not expected.

topics.title: Shop, Market, and Bargaining
topics.intro: You'll be able to ask a price, politely bargain at a market, and turn down extras. You'll also learn how to get a tax refund (tax free) when you fly out and where to complain if you've been cheated.

phrases.note: Say it with a smile: at a market that's the start of bargaining, not an insult.
Helps with persistent sellers.
Name your own price. If the price doesn't suit you, you can calmly walk away.
For several items sellers give a discount more readily.

phrases.ru: May I try it on (try it)?

phrases.py: Yǒu dà yí hào de ma?
phrases.ru: Do you have one size bigger?
phrases.note: Chinese sizes often run small.
Foreign cards aren't accepted everywhere; check before buying.

phrases.ru: Can I get tax free here?
phrases.note: Look for the sign 离境退税 / Tax Refund.
For a tax refund you need the 发票 and the form 退税申请单 (tuìshuì shēnqǐngdān).
Keep your receipt: 小票 (xiǎopiào).
You'll hear this at the checkout. Bags cost extra. The answer: 不要 or 要一个.

phrases.ru: Do you have a loyalty card?
phrases.note: You'll hear this at the checkout. The answer: 没有 (méiyǒu), meaning “no.”
You'll hear this at the market. Often it's not the end of the bargaining yet.

phrases.ru: So how much will you give?
phrases.note: You'll hear this when the seller invites you to name your own price.
You'll hear this when paying.
You'll hear this in a shop: open the payment QR code in Alipay or WeChat Pay, and the cashier will scan it.

dialogue.zh: 看一看！喜欢吗？
dialogue.py: Kàn yi kàn! Xǐhuan ma?
dialogue.ru: Look! Do you like it?

dialogue.zh: 这个多少钱？
dialogue.py: Zhège duōshao qián?
dialogue.ru: How much is this?

dialogue.zh: 两百。
dialogue.py: Liǎngbǎi.
dialogue.ru: Two hundred.

dialogue.zh: 太贵了！一百，行吗？
dialogue.py: Tài guì le! Yìbǎi, xíng ma?
dialogue.ru: Too expensive! A hundred, okay?

dialogue.zh: 不能再便宜了。一百八。
dialogue.py: Bù néng zài piányi le. Yìbǎi bā.
dialogue.ru: I can't go any cheaper. A hundred eighty.

dialogue.zh: 我就看看。谢谢。
dialogue.py: Wǒ jiù kànkan. Xièxie.
dialogue.ru: I'm just looking. Thanks.

dialogue.zh: 好好好，一百五！
dialogue.py: Hǎo hǎo hǎo, yìbǎi wǔ!
dialogue.ru: Okay, okay, a hundred fifty!

dialogue.zh: 一百二，我就要了。
dialogue.py: Yìbǎi èr, wǒ jiù yào le.
dialogue.ru: A hundred twenty, and I'll take it.

dialogue.zh: 行，扫这儿。
dialogue.py: Xíng, sǎo zhèr.
dialogue.ru: Deal, scan here.

topics.culture: People bargain at markets, in souvenir stalls, and at clothing markets; in supermarkets, chain stores, and shopping malls the prices are fixed. Bargaining is a game: smile, name your own price, and don't be afraid to walk away; you'll often be called back with a new offer. If you named a price and the seller agreed, it's customary to complete the purchase. Tourist markets have many copies of famous brands, so don't expect them to be original.

tips.t: Bargaining is appropriate at markets and in souvenir stalls; the first price quoted to a tourist is often inflated. In chain stores, malls, and pharmacies prices are fixed, and no one bargains there.
Ask the price, say 太贵了, and name your own. If you can't agree, say thank you and leave. You can compare the price in the Taobao (淘宝) or Pinduoduo (拼多多) apps.
Since 2008, supermarkets, shops, and markets may not give out plastic bags for free; their cost is rung up separately. Bring your own bag.

Since February 1, 2026, a People's Bank of China rule is in effect: a seller may not refuse cash yuan (except where the law requires cashless payment). If they refuse, you can contact the city line 12345.

VAT refund for a foreigner: a purchase of 200 yuan or more in one day in one store with the 离境退税 / Tax Refund sign, with the goods unused and taken out of the country within 90 days. You get back 11% or 8% of the amount minus the agent's 2% fee; up to 20,000 yuan can be received in cash.

Get the 发票 and the 退税申请单 form from the store. Before checking in your luggage, show your purchases, receipts, and passport to customs, then after the check you'll receive the money at the refund counter. In 2026 the procedure is being moved to electronic form, and since September 1, 2026 “refund right at purchase” (即买即退) has been expanded; ask in the store.
Keep your receipts. Complaints about a seller are taken by the consumer rights protection hotline 12315; tourism complaints, by line 12301.
In Beijing the city line 12345 connects you to an operator in a foreign language; among its 8 languages is Russian. In other cities the set of languages may differ.

quiz.q: Where is bargaining NOT customary?
quiz.explain: In chain stores and shopping malls, prices are fixed.

quiz.q: From what amount in one store in one day can you get tax free?
quiz.explain: Since 2025 the threshold has been lowered from 500 to 200 yuan (purchases in one day in one store).

quiz.q: The cashier asks “要袋子吗？”. What does it mean?
options: Do you have a loyalty card?
quiz.explain: 袋子 means bag; bags cost extra in China.

quiz.q: A seller refuses to take cash yuan. What is true?
options: He's right: cash isn't accepted in China
Since February 1, 2026, refusal is prohibited, and you can complain to 12345
You have to pay an extra fee
quiz.explain: The PBOC's 2026 rules prohibit refusing cash, and complaints are accepted, among others, by city hotlines.

topics.title: Hotel, Check-in, and Police
topics.intro: After this topic you'll check in to a hotel, understand the front desk's questions, and be able to ask for help if something is wrong in your room. We'll also cover the mandatory registration of foreigners: at a hotel they do it for you.

phrases.note: Show the booking confirmation on your screen.
They won't check in a foreigner without a passport: it's used for registration.
Put in your own name; it's better to show how it's written in the booking in Latin letters.
退房 (tuìfáng) means checking out of the room.
The password is often written on a card with the key.

phrases.ru: There's a problem in the room.
phrases.note: Then show what's wrong, or use the phrases below.
Ask when booking, especially in small guesthouses.
The deposit is usually held through Alipay or WeChat and returned at check-out.
In short: 早餐？(zǎocān?) means “breakfast?”
坏了 (huài le) means “it's broken”: put in any object and point at it.

phrases.ru: Can I leave my luggage in storage?
phrases.note: Handy on check-out day if your train or flight is in the evening.

phrases.py: Qǐng gěi wǒ jiǔdiàn de míngpiàn.
phrases.ru: Please give me the hotel's business card.
phrases.note: The card has the address in Chinese; you can show it to a taxi driver.
Then you need to complete the registration yourself or together with the host within 24 hours.

phrases.ru: I've come to register my stay.
phrases.note: Said at the police station 派出所 (pàichūsuǒ) if you're not staying at a hotel.
You'll hear this at the front desk. The answer: 有 (yǒu), meaning “yes, I do.”

phrases.ru: How many nights will you be staying with us?
phrases.note: You'll hear this. Show the number on your fingers or in the booking.

phrases.ru: The deposit is two hundred yuan.
phrases.note: You'll hear this. The amount is different at each hotel.
You'll hear this. 房卡 (fángkǎ) means key card.

phrases.ru: Breakfast is on the second floor.
phrases.note: You'll hear this. 楼 (lóu) means floor.
You'll hear this. The check-out time is different at each hotel.

dialogue.zh: 您好！请问有预订吗？
dialogue.py: Nín hǎo! Qǐngwèn yǒu yùdìng ma?
dialogue.ru: Hello! Do you have a reservation?

dialogue.zh: 有。我叫伊万，这是我的护照。
dialogue.py: Yǒu. Wǒ jiào Yīwàn, zhè shì wǒ de hùzhào.

dialogue.zh: 好的，住三晚，对吗？
dialogue.py: Hǎo de, zhù sān wǎn, duì ma?
dialogue.ru: Okay, three nights, right?

dialogue.zh: 对。我要去派出所登记吗？
dialogue.py: Duì. Wǒ yào qù pàichūsuǒ dēngjì ma?
dialogue.ru: Yes. Do I need to go register with the police?

dialogue.zh: 不用，我们帮您登记。押金两百。
dialogue.py: Bú yòng, wǒmen bāng nín dēngjì. Yājīn liǎngbǎi.
dialogue.ru: No need, we'll register you. The deposit is two hundred yuan.

dialogue.zh: 可以用支付宝吗？
dialogue.py: Kěyǐ yòng Zhīfùbǎo ma?
dialogue.ru: Can I pay with Alipay?

dialogue.zh: 可以。这是房卡，早餐在二楼。
dialogue.py: Kěyǐ. Zhè shì fángkǎ, zǎocān zài èr lóu.
dialogue.ru: Yes, you can. Here is your key card; breakfast is on the second floor.

dialogue.zh: 谢谢！几点退房？
dialogue.py: Xièxie! Jǐ diǎn tuìfáng?
dialogue.ru: Thank you! What time is check-out?

dialogue.zh: 中午十二点。
dialogue.py: Zhōngwǔ shí'èr diǎn.
dialogue.ru: At twelve noon.

topics.culture: Every foreigner in China must be registered at their place of stay, and this also applies to those who entered without a visa. At a hotel it's simple: the front desk takes your passport and passes the data to the police itself, so you don't need to go anywhere. If you're staying with friends or in an apartment, you must register within 24 hours, at the local police station 派出所 or online where that's already available. At check-in almost everywhere they take a deposit (usually through Alipay or WeChat) and return it at check-out, and in room numbers the digit 1 is often pronounced “yāo.” Keep your passport with you: the police have the right to check the documents of any foreigner over 16.

tips.t: If you're staying at a hotel, the hotel handles the registration. If you're staying with friends or in an apartment, you or the host must register with the police at your place of residence within 24 hours of check-in.
Registration at your place of stay is mandatory also for those who entered without a visa.

Since March 20, 2026, registration outside a hotel can be completed online through the “移民局12367” app, its mini-programs in WeChat and Alipay, or the NIA website; so far in 7 regions (Hebei, Liaoning, Zhejiang, Hubei, Guangxi, Chongqing, Sichuan). It's promised to be extended to the whole country later.
A foreigner who fails to register at their place of stay outside a hotel faces a warning and a fine of up to 2,000 yuan.

tips.h: A hotel can't refuse because of a “license”
tips.t: According to a clarification from the Ministry of Public Security, a hotel may not refuse a foreigner on the pretext that it has no “permit for foreigners.” In Shanghai the police confirm: all of the city's hotels can register foreigners.
Foreigners over 16 must carry their passport with them and show it to the police on request. Take a photo of your passport and of the page with the entry stamp.
Before check-out they'll check the minibar in the room, after which the deposit is released. Save a screenshot of the deposit hold in the app.
Take the hotel's business card or save the address in Chinese: a taxi driver or passerby will understand it right away.
Police: 110, fire: 119, ambulance: 120, traffic accidents: 122. Calls are free.
The information line of the National Immigration Administration, 12367, also works in Russian: choose the language in the voice menu.

quiz.q: You're staying with a friend in an apartment. What do you need to do?
options: Nothing, registration is only for those with visas
Register within 24 hours with the police or online where available
quiz.explain: Outside a hotel, you or the host register within 24 hours, at the 派出所 or online in regions where that already works.

quiz.q: How do you ask what time hotel check-out is?
quiz.explain: 退房 means check-out, vacating the room.

quiz.q: How do you tell the front desk “The air conditioner is broken”?
quiz.explain: 坏了 means “it's broken”; 空调 means air conditioner.

quiz.q: The front desk says: “押金两百.” What does it mean?
options: The room costs two hundred yuan
The deposit is two hundred yuan
quiz.explain: 押金 means deposit, 两百 means two hundred.

topics.intro: You'll be able to find a toilet, understand the answer “straight—right—left,” and read the main signs. You'll also learn simple rules of the city: where smoking is not allowed, what water to drink, and who to call if you need help.

phrases.note: The most needed phrase. You can show it on your screen.
Sounds more polite, suitable for a restaurant and a hotel.
Characters on toilet doors: 男 for men, 女 for women.
A public toilet may not have paper.
Ask in a café or a shop.

phrases.note: Put in a place or show an address: 地铁站 (dìtiězhàn) means metro station.
Show your hotel's address in characters.
Ask in temples, museums, and before photographing people.
In a crowd, the metro, a narrow passage.
A 便利店 has water, tissues, chargers, and often hot food too.
In hotels, at train stations, and on trains boiling water is often free.
You'll hear this and see a hand gesture.

You'll hear this at a train station, a museum, at the ticket window.
A sign. Follow it, especially in museums, temples, government buildings, and at protected sites.
A sign. 吸烟 is the formal word for “to smoke”; in conversation it's 抽烟.
A sign at entrances and in restrooms.

dialogue.zh: 不好意思，请问，厕所在哪儿？
dialogue.py: Bù hǎoyìsi, qǐngwèn, cèsuǒ zài nǎr?
dialogue.ru: Excuse me, where is the toilet?

dialogue.py: Zài nàbiān, yìzhí zǒu, ránhòu yòu guǎi.
dialogue.ru: Over there: straight ahead, then right.

dialogue.zh: 对不起，请说慢一点。
dialogue.py: Duìbuqǐ, qǐng shuō màn yìdiǎn.
dialogue.ru: Sorry, please speak more slowly.

dialogue.zh: 一直走……右拐。
dialogue.py: Yìzhí zǒu… yòu guǎi.
dialogue.ru: Straight… right.

dialogue.zh: 谢谢！里面有纸吗？
dialogue.py: Xièxie! Lǐmiàn yǒu zhǐ ma?
dialogue.ru: Thank you! And is there paper there?

dialogue.zh: 可能没有。我这儿有，给你。
dialogue.py: Kěnéng méiyǒu. Wǒ zhèr yǒu, gěi nǐ.
dialogue.ru: There may not be. I have some, here you go.

dialogue.zh: 太谢谢了！
dialogue.py: Tài xièxie le!
dialogue.ru: Thank you so much!

dialogue.zh: 不客气！
dialogue.py: Bú kèqi!
dialogue.ru: You're welcome!

topics.culture: Public toilets are common in Chinese cities and are usually free, but many have squat toilets (蹲坑, dūnkēng), and there may be no paper. Shopping malls, hotels, and new metro stations also have the familiar sit-down toilets; look for the symbol on the stall door. In the metro, at train stations, and at sights people stand in lines and go through bag screening. Speaking loudly is normal, but getting angry and raising your voice at staff means “losing face.” Questions about age, family, and salary are ordinary curiosity, not tactlessness.

tips.t: Carry paper tissues and wet wipes or hand sanitizer in your pocket: public toilets may have no paper or soap.
If there's a bin next to the toilet, the paper goes in it: in old buildings the plumbing can get clogged.
Tap water is drunk only boiled; you can brush your teeth with it. Bottled water is sold everywhere, about 2 yuan a bottle.

In Beijing, smoking is banned indoors in public places, at work, and on public transport; the fine is 50 yuan, and up to 200 if you refuse to stop. Other cities have their own rules; go by the 禁止吸烟 signs.
禁止拍照 means no photos, 禁止吸烟 means no smoking, 禁止入内 (jìnzhǐ rùnèi) means no entry. If you're asked not to take photos, put your phone away and don't argue.
Police: 110, fire: 119, ambulance: 120, traffic accidents: 122. Calls are free throughout the country, and false calls are prohibited.

If you need information or help in a non-emergency, call 12345. In Beijing you'll be connected to an operator in a foreign language; among its 8 languages is Russian; in Zhejiang, English on weekdays.
Questions and complaints about tourism services are handled by the national line 12301.

quiz.q: How do you ask where the toilet is?
quiz.explain: 厕所在哪儿 means “Where is the toilet?”. More politely: 洗手间在哪儿？

quiz.q: What does the sign “禁止拍照” mean?
quiz.explain: 拍照 means to take photos, 禁止 means prohibited.

quiz.q: What number do you call for an ambulance?
quiz.explain: 120 is an ambulance, 110 is the police, 119 is the fire department, 122 is traffic accidents.

quiz.q: What is true about smoking in Beijing?
options: Smoking is banned indoors in public places and on transport
It's banned only in the metro
quiz.explain: Beijing's smoking control rules: a ban indoors in public places, at work, and on transport, with a fine of up to 200 yuan.

role.ai_role: a security guard in a city park in Shanghai, good-natured; he speaks very slowly and in short HSK 1 level phrases, and shows the direction with his hand

Ask where the toilet is
Ask them to speak more slowly
Understand “straight” and “right/left”

topics.title: Pharmacy, Doctor, and Hospital
topics.intro: After this topic you'll be able to buy a simple medicine at a pharmacy, show where it hurts, and understand the main questions from a pharmacist or doctor. It also covers what to do if you need a hospital and how not to be left without your own medicines.

phrases.note: A universal phrase. Then show where it hurts.
Point to the spot with your hand; that's enough.
A pharmacy is easy to find by the sign 药店 or 药房.

phrases.ru: I need to go to the hospital.
phrases.note: In a taxi, show the driver the hospital's name on your screen.
The template: 我对……过敏. Look up the word for your own allergy in advance and save it on your phone.
Show a photo of the packaging and the name of the active ingredient in Latin letters.

phrases.ru: How many times a day should I take it?
How many tablets at a time?

处方 means prescription.

phrases.py: Yǒu huì shuō Yīngyǔ de yīshēng ma?
phrases.ru: Is there a doctor who speaks English?
What seems to be the problem?

You'll hear this. The answer: 没有 (méiyǒu) means no, or 有 and show the name on your phone.
You'll hear this. At a hospital, tests and appointments are often paid for in advance, at the cashier or on your phone.

phrases.ru: You'd better go to the hospital.

dialogue.zh: 你好，哪里不舒服？
dialogue.py: Nǐ hǎo, nǎli bù shūfu?
dialogue.ru: Hello, what seems to be the problem?

dialogue.zh: 我发烧了，头也疼。
dialogue.py: Wǒ fāshāo le, tóu yě téng.
dialogue.ru: I have a fever and a headache.

dialogue.zh: 有没有过敏？
dialogue.py: Yǒu méiyǒu guòmǐn?
dialogue.ru: Do you have any allergies?

dialogue.zh: 没有。有退烧药吗？
dialogue.py: Méiyǒu. Yǒu tuìshāoyào ma?
dialogue.ru: No. Do you have a fever reducer?

dialogue.zh: 有，这个。按说明书吃。
dialogue.py: Yǒu, zhège. Àn shuōmíngshū chī.
dialogue.ru: Yes, here. Take it according to the instructions.

dialogue.zh: 饭前还是饭后？
dialogue.py: Fànqián háishi fànhòu?
dialogue.ru: Before or after meals?

dialogue.py: Fànhòu. Míngtiān hái fāshāo de huà, qù yīyuàn kànkan ba.
dialogue.ru: After. If your fever doesn't go away tomorrow, go to the hospital.

dialogue.zh: 好的。多少钱？
dialogue.py: Hǎo de. Duōshao qián?
dialogue.ru: Okay. How much is it?

dialogue.zh: 二十八块，扫这里。
dialogue.py: Èrshíbā kuài, sǎo zhèli.
dialogue.ru: 28 yuan, scan here.

topics.culture: For minor ailments in China you go to a pharmacy (药店): there is one on almost every street, and the pharmacist will ask what hurts and whether you have allergies. Medicines are divided into prescription and over-the-counter ones; the packaging of over-the-counter ones has an OTC mark. If you need a doctor, you go straight to a hospital (医院): first registration (挂号) at the right department, then the appointment, payment for tests, and the tests themselves. In big cities, hospitals sometimes have international departments (国际部), which are more expensive but have English. Instructions for medicines are in Chinese, so photograph the packaging and translate it with a photo translator. If a life is in danger, call 120.

tips.t: The ambulance number is 120 (police: 110, fire: 119). Save your hotel's address in Chinese so you can give it to the dispatcher or show it to a passerby.

You may bring in a small quantity of medicines for personal use, in a reasonable amount; customs may inspect them. Narcotic and strong psychotropic drugs require a medical certificate and a quantity of no more than one prescription.

By the rules, prescription medicines are sold only with a doctor's prescription, and the packaging of over-the-counter ones must carry the OTC mark. If you aren't given the medicine you need without a prescription, it isn't the pharmacy's whim, it's the rule.

Foreigners pay for treatment themselves or through commercial insurance. Direct billing with the insurer is possible only if your insurer is on the specific hospital's list, so check in advance; you'll need your passport and policy.

tips.h: How you pay at a hospital
tips.t: For example, Beijing hospitals accept cash yuan, international cards (Visa, Mastercard, etc.), UnionPay, WeChat Pay, and Alipay from foreigners, and prices are the same as for locals. In other cities, check on the spot.
In Beijing you can book through the 114 platform (the International Service Beijing / 京通 service) in a WeChat or Alipay mini-program, which has English.
Big cities have international clinics and hospital departments with round-the-clock phone lines and English-speaking staff. Find the one closest to your hotel before your trip.
Take photos of your medicines and write down the active ingredient in Latin letters: with it a pharmacist will find an equivalent faster.

When you go to a hospital, take your passport and insurance policy: without a passport direct billing with the insurer can't be arranged, and the document may also be requested at appointment registration.

quiz.q: What number do you call for an ambulance in China?
quiz.explain: 120 is an ambulance, 110 is the police, 119 is the fire department, 122 is traffic accidents.

quiz.q: How do you show a pharmacist where it hurts?
quiz.explain: 这里疼 means “it hurts here.” Say it and point with your hand.

quiz.q: The pharmacist asks “有没有过敏？”. What is he asking about?
quiz.explain: 过敏 means allergy. The answer: 没有 (no) or 有 + the name.

quiz.q: Can you bring your own medicines to China?
options: Yes, a small quantity for yourself; strong ones with a doctor's certificate
No, no medicines may be brought in
Yes, in any quantity and without inspection
Only if you send them by mail
quiz.explain: For personal use, a reasonable amount; narcotic and strong psychotropic drugs require a certificate and no more than one prescription.

role.ai_role: Chína is a pharmacist at a pharmacy near the hotel in Shanghai. She speaks very simply and slowly, in HSK 1–2 level phrases, asks one question at a time, and waits for the answer.
role.user_goal: explain what hurts, buy a fever reducer, and find out how to take it
role.opening: 你好！哪里不舒服？
checklist: Say what hurts (我发烧了 / 我头疼 / 这里疼)
Answer about allergies (没有 / 我对……过敏)
Ask about a medicine (有……吗？)
Clarify how to take it (一天吃几次 / 饭前还是饭后)
Ask the price and say thank you

topics.title: Emergencies
topics.intro: After this topic you'll know who to call and what to say if something happens: call for help, call the police or an ambulance, and explain where you are. And most importantly, the step-by-step procedure if your passport is lost.

phrases.note: Shout it only in real danger.
Police: 110.
Ambulance: 120.
Fire department: 119.
Say it right away: the dispatcher will understand that an interpreter is needed.

phrases.py: Wǒ de shǒujī bèi tōu le.
Wǒ de qiánbāo bèi tōu le.

phrases.note: Show the point on the map on your phone or send your location in WeChat.
For the 12367 line: it has Russian.

phrases.zh: 我要联系俄罗斯大使馆。
phrases.ru: I need to contact the Russian embassy.
phrases.note: A consulate is 领事馆 (lǐngshìguǎn).

phrases.ru: Please give me a confirmation of the report.
phrases.note: 报案回执 is a receipt confirming that you reported the loss. You need it for the next steps.

phrases.zh: 能借你的手机打个电话吗？
phrases.py: Néng jiè nǐ de shǒujī dǎ ge diànhuà ma?
phrases.ru: May I make a call from your phone?

phrases.note: You'll hear this. The first question from a dispatcher and a police officer.
You'll hear this. Give the street and a landmark or show a map.
You'll hear this. The answer: 没有 (méiyǒu) means no; 有 means yes.
You'll hear this. It means the police or an ambulance are already on their way to you.

dialogue.zh: 110，请讲。发生什么事了？
dialogue.py: Yāo yāo líng, qǐng jiǎng. Fāshēng shénme shì le?
dialogue.ru: 110, go ahead. What happened?

dialogue.zh: 你好，我是俄罗斯人。我的护照被偷了。
dialogue.py: Nǐ hǎo, wǒ shì Éluósīrén. Wǒ de hùzhào bèi tōu le.
dialogue.ru: Hello, I'm from Russia. My passport was stolen.

dialogue.zh: 你有没有受伤？
dialogue.py: Nǐ yǒu méiyǒu shòushāng?
dialogue.ru: Are you injured?

dialogue.zh: 没有。
dialogue.py: Méiyǒu.
dialogue.ru: No.

dialogue.zh: 你在哪儿？
dialogue.py: Nǐ zài nǎr?
dialogue.ru: Where are you?

dialogue.zh: 我在人民广场地铁站二号口。
dialogue.py: Wǒ zài Rénmín Guǎngchǎng dìtiězhàn èr hào kǒu.
dialogue.ru: I'm at Exit 2 of People's Square metro station.

dialogue.zh: 好，请在原地等，警察马上到。
dialogue.py: Hǎo, qǐng zài yuándì děng, jǐngchá mǎshàng dào.
dialogue.ru: Okay, wait where you are, the police will arrive shortly.

dialogue.zh: 请说慢一点。
dialogue.py: Qǐng shuō màn yìdiǎn.
dialogue.ru: Please speak more slowly.

dialogue.zh: 好。在原地，等警察。
dialogue.py: Hǎo. Zài yuándì, děng jǐngchá.
dialogue.ru: Okay. Stay where you are and wait for the police.

topics.culture: Emergency numbers in China: 110 is the police, 120 is an ambulance, 119 is the fire department, 122 is traffic accidents. Tell the dispatcher first what happened and where you are: the street, metro station, hotel name, or a landmark. Keep your hotel's address in Chinese in your phone's notes, and know how to send your location in WeChat. If your passport is lost, the order is this: the police where it was lost → the police Exit and Entry department (出入境) for a loss certificate → the Russian embassy or consulate general for a new document → 出入境 again for a visa or exit permit. Photograph your passport page and entry stamp in advance: copies speed up every step.

tips.t: 110 is the police, 120 is an ambulance, 119 is the fire department, 122 is the traffic police (accidents).

The hotline of the National Immigration Administration, 12367, works around the clock, and you can choose Russian in the voice menu. From abroad: +86-12367. It helps with questions about visas, stay, and documents.
Go straight to the police station (派出所) where it was lost or stolen and report it. Ask for a confirmation of the report (报案回执) with your name on it.

With the police certificate, go to the Exit and Entry department (出入境) for a certificate of loss of a foreigner's passport. You usually need an application form, photographs, and copies of the lost passport and visa, if you have them.
With the loss certificate, go to the Russian embassy or consulate general: they will issue a new passport or a certificate for returning to Russia.

With the new document, go to 出入境 again for a visa or exit permit. For example, Shenzhen's rules require you to complete this within 30 days of the date of the loss report; check the procedure and deadlines in your city with 12367.
Before your trip, save the addresses and phone numbers of the Russian embassy in Beijing and the consulates general from the official list of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Photograph your passport's photo page and entry stamp, keep the photos on your phone and in the cloud, and keep a paper copy separate from your passport.
Save your hotel's address in characters and learn to send your location in WeChat: “+” → Location (位置).

quiz.q: What number do you call for the police in China?
quiz.explain: 110 is the police. 120 is an ambulance, 119 is the fire department, 12306 is the railway.

quiz.q: Your passport was stolen. What should you do first?
options: Wait at the hotel until the passport turns up
Report it to the police (派出所) where it was stolen and get a confirmation
quiz.explain: First the police and the 报案回执, then 出入境, the embassy, and 出入境 again.

quiz.q: What should you say first to the 110 dispatcher?
options: What happened and where you are
How many days you've been in China
quiz.explain: What happened and the exact place are the most important things: that way help arrives faster.

quiz.q: How do you ask for service in Russian on the 12367 line?
quiz.explain: 俄语 means the Russian language, 服务 means service. In the 12367 voice menu you can also choose Russian.

Say that you're from Russia (我是俄罗斯人)
Answer whether you're injured (没有 / 有)
Give the place or a landmark (我在……)
Ask them to speak more slowly or ask for an interpreter

topics.title: If You're Staying Long: Renting and Registration
topics.intro: After this topic you'll be able to view and rent an apartment, ask about the price and deposit, and complete your residence registration on time. This will come in handy if you're not staying at a hotel: in an apartment, with friends, or through a short-term rental app.

phrases.ru: I want to rent an apartment.

phrases.note: 押金 means security deposit, deposit.

phrases.ru: I need to complete my residence registration.
phrases.note: Show this phrase to the landlord and at the police station (派出所).
Point at the item: 这个坏了 means “this is broken.”

phrases.ru: A one-month deposit and rent paid three months in advance.
phrases.note: You'll hear this. A common rental condition. There's also 押一付一: a one-month deposit and monthly payment.

phrases.ru: How much is the agency's commission?
phrases.note: The agency must state its price in advance.

phrases.ru: How do I pay for water and electricity?
Is the property management fee included?
phrases.note: 物业 (wùyè) means the building's management company.

phrases.ru: Can I see the property ownership document?
phrases.note: This way you make sure the apartment is being rented out by someone who has the right to do so.

phrases.py: Nǐ néng péi wǒ qù pàichūsuǒ ma?
phrases.ru: Could you go to the police station with me?
phrases.note: For registration: with the landlord, everything goes more easily.

phrases.ru: When will the deposit be returned?
Do you have your passport with you?

phrases.note: You'll hear this. The answer: 一个月 (yí ge yuè) means one month, 三个月 means three months, 一年 (yì nián) means one year.
You'll hear this. If you hear it, check the contract: cases where the deposit may be withheld must be spelled out in it.
You'll hear this. For breakdowns in the building's common areas and for noise, people usually go to the 物业.

dialogue.zh: 四千，押一付三。

dialogue.zh: 可以月付吗？

dialogue.zh: 可以，月付四千二。

dialogue.zh: 好。可以看一下房产证吗？
dialogue.py: Hǎo. Kěyǐ kàn yíxià fángchǎnzhèng ma?
dialogue.ru: Okay. Can I see the property ownership document?

dialogue.zh: 可以，这是房产证。
dialogue.py: Kěyǐ, zhè shì fángchǎnzhèng.
dialogue.ru: Yes, here it is.

dialogue.zh: 我是外国人，要办住宿登记。你能陪我去派出所吗？
dialogue.py: Wǒ shì wàiguórén, yào bàn zhùsù dēngjì. Nǐ néng péi wǒ qù pàichūsuǒ ma?
dialogue.ru: I'm a foreigner, I need to register. Will you go to the station with me?

dialogue.zh: 没问题，签完合同就去。
dialogue.py: Méi wèntí, qiānwán hétong jiù qù.
dialogue.ru: No problem, we'll sign the contract and go right away.

topics.culture: Apartments in China are most often rented through agencies and rental apps; a common condition is 押一付三 (a one-month deposit and three months paid in advance), but with a landlord you can agree on monthly payment. The main rule for a foreigner: if you're not staying at a hotel, within 24 hours of moving in you must complete your residence registration (住宿登记) at the local police station (派出所), and in some regions already online. At a hotel, the hotel does this itself. When you move in, photograph defects and meter readings: that's the best argument when getting your deposit back. Noise and breakdowns in the building are handled through the management company (物业) or the residents' chat in WeChat.

tips.t: Russian citizens with a regular passport can enter China visa-free for up to 30 days (tourism, business, relatives and friends, exchanges, transit); the arrangement has been extended until December 31, 2027. If you plan to stay longer, to work or study, get a visa of the right category in advance at a Chinese embassy or visa center.

If you're not staying at a hotel (an apartment, with friends), you must register within 24 hours of moving in; you or the host do this. The rule also applies to those who arrived without a visa, and it repeats each time you move.

Since March 20, 2026, in pilot regions (Hebei, Liaoning, Zhejiang, Hubei, Guangxi, Chongqing, Sichuan) registration can be completed online: on the NIA website, in the 移民局12367 app, or its mini-programs in WeChat and Alipay. Online registration has the same force as in-person registration; in other regions go to the 派出所.
For failing to register, the law provides for a warning or a fine of up to 2,000 yuan.

tips.h: Check who is renting it out
tips.t: Under the “Housing Rental Regulations” (in effect since September 15, 2025), the landlord must show documents confirming the right to rent out the apartment. Ask for them before signing the contract.

The deposit amount, the return deadline, and the cases where it may be withheld must be spelled out in the contract; a deposit can't be withheld without grounds. Read this clause in a translator before signing.
The agency must state its prices openly and in advance. Ask for the commission amount before viewing the apartment.
Photograph all defects, furniture, appliances, and meter readings on the day you move in and send the photos to the landlord in WeChat: that way you'll have dated proof.
Questions about your visa, length of stay, and registration can be asked on the NIA line 12367 (around the clock, with Russian available).

quiz.q: You've rented an apartment. Within what period must you complete residence registration?
options: Only if you live there longer than a month
quiz.explain: A foreigner not staying at a hotel registers within 24 hours, either on their own or through the landlord.

quiz.q: The landlord says “押一付三.” What does it mean?
options: A 1-month deposit and payment for 3 months in advance
quiz.explain: 押 means security deposit, 付 means to pay.

quiz.q: Why ask to see the 房产证?
options: To make sure the apartment is being rented out by someone who has the right to do so
To find out how much the internet costs
To get the keys to the building entrance
quiz.explain: 房产证 is the property ownership document. The landlord must show documents proving the right to rent out the housing.

quiz.q: The elevator in your building is broken, and the neighbors make noise at night. Who do you contact?
options: The 物业, the management company
quiz.explain: 物业 is responsible for the building and order in it.

role.ai_role: Chína is the owner of an apartment in Hangzhou. She speaks very simply and slowly, in HSK 1–2 level phrases, states the price in numbers, and readily agrees to help with registration.
role.user_goal: find out the price and deposit, agree on monthly payment, and ask for help with registration
role.opening: 你好！这就是房子。你看看。
checklist: Ask the monthly price (一个月多少钱)
Ask about the deposit (押金多少)
Ask to pay monthly (可以月付吗)
Ask to see the 房产证
Ask for help with registration (住宿登记 / 派出所)

tracks.title: Work: Office and Career
tracks.ru: Chinese for working at a Chinese company: from interviews and meetings to WeChat messaging, company parties, and knowing how to politely say “no.”

topics.title: The Interview and Talking About Yourself
topics.intro: You need this when you're looking for a job in China through BOSS直聘, LinkedIn, or a referral and going through interviews with HR and your future manager. Learn to introduce yourself briefly, talk about your experience and strengths, and discuss salary, visa, and the probation period.

phrases.zh: 您好，我叫安娜，来自俄罗斯。
phrases.py: Nín hǎo, wǒ jiào Ānnà, láizì Éluósī.
phrases.ru: Hello, my name is Anna, I'm from Russia.
phrases.note: In an interview, address people with “您” until you're offered otherwise.

phrases.py: Wǒ yǒu wǔ nián de xiāoshòu jīngyàn.
phrases.ru: I have five years of sales experience.

phrases.zh: 我之前在一家物流公司负责俄罗斯市场。
phrases.py: Wǒ zhīqián zài yì jiā wùliú gōngsī fùzé Éluósī shìchǎng.
phrases.ru: Previously, at a logistics company, I was responsible for the Russian market.
phrases.note: 负责 + a field is the main verb for describing responsibilities.

phrases.zh: 我毕业于莫斯科国立大学，专业是国际贸易。
phrases.py: Wǒ bìyè yú Mòsīkē Guólì Dàxué, zhuānyè shì guójì màoyì.
phrases.ru: I graduated from Moscow State University, majoring in international trade.
phrases.note: 毕业于… is a formal but very appropriate construction for an interview.

phrases.zh: 我的中文是HSK五级，工作沟通没问题。
phrases.py: Wǒ de Zhōngwén shì HSK wǔ jí, gōngzuò gōutōng méi wèntí.
phrases.ru: I have HSK 5, and communicating at work is no problem.

phrases.zh: 我的优点是沟通能力强，适应得快。
phrases.py: Wǒ de yōudiǎn shì gōutōng nénglì qiáng, shìyìng de kuài.
phrases.ru: My strengths are strong communication skills and quick adaptation.

phrases.zh: 我的缺点是有时候太追求细节。
phrases.py: Wǒ de quēdiǎn shì yǒu shíhou tài zhuīqiú xìjié.
phrases.ru: My weakness is that I sometimes get too caught up in details.
phrases.note: The classic “safe” answer to the question about weaknesses.

phrases.zh: 请问这个岗位主要负责什么？
phrases.py: Qǐngwèn zhège gǎngwèi zhǔyào fùzé shénme?
phrases.ru: Could you tell me what this position mainly involves?

phrases.zh: 我很看好贵公司在俄罗斯市场的发展。
phrases.py: Wǒ hěn kànhǎo guì gōngsī zài Éluósī shìchǎng de fāzhǎn.
phrases.ru: I believe in your company's prospects in the Russian market.
phrases.note: 贵公司 is the polite “your company”; that's what people say in interviews and business letters.

phrases.zh: 我的期望薪资是每月两万左右，可以商量。
phrases.py: Wǒ de qīwàng xīnzī shì měi yuè liǎng wàn zuǒyòu, kěyǐ shāngliang.
phrases.ru: My expected salary is around 20,000 yuan a month, and I'm open to discussion.
phrases.note: Salary in China is discussed by the month (月薪), usually before tax (税前). Social insurance contributions (社保) are deducted from it too: foreigners working in China also take part in it by law.

phrases.zh: 请问公司能帮忙办工作签证吗？
phrases.py: Qǐngwèn gōngsī néng bāngmáng bàn gōngzuò qiānzhèng ma?
phrases.ru: Can the company help with a work visa?
phrases.note: “工作签证” is the colloquial name for the whole package. The employer obtains a work permit (外国人工作许可), on the basis of which a Z work visa is issued, and after entry you need to get a residence permit for work within 30 days (HR usually helps).

phrases.ru: How long is the probation period?
phrases.note: By law it depends on the length of the contract: up to 1 month for a contract of 3 months to 1 year, up to 2 months for 1 to 3 years, up to 6 months for 3 years or more or an open-ended contract.

phrases.zh: 一年是几薪？有年终奖吗？
phrases.py: Yì nián shì jǐ xīn? Yǒu niánzhōngjiǎng ma?
phrases.ru: How many months of salary a year? Is there an annual bonus?
phrases.note: “13薪” and “14薪” show how many months of salary are paid per year, including the bonus.

phrases.zh: 我什么时候能知道面试结果？
phrases.py: Wǒ shénme shíhou néng zhīdào miànshì jiéguǒ?
phrases.ru: When will I find out the interview result?

phrases.zh: 谢谢您给我这次面试机会。
phrases.py: Xièxie nín gěi wǒ zhè cì miànshì jīhuì.
phrases.ru: Thank you for giving me this interview opportunity.

dialogue.zh: 你好，请坐。先简单介绍一下你自己吧。
dialogue.py: Nǐ hǎo, qǐng zuò. Xiān jiǎndān jièshào yíxià nǐ zìjǐ ba.
dialogue.ru: Hello, please have a seat. To start, tell me briefly about yourself.

dialogue.zh: 您好，我叫伊万，来自俄罗斯，在中国工作三年了，之前做跨境电商运营。
